Count and Noncount Nouns: Picture Quantifiers

Look at the picture. Choose the correct word.

Level 2 — Grammar Review

 

Count or Noncount?

Look at each picture. Say the word. Is it a count noun or a noncount noun?

Count: you can say one, two, three … It has a plural.
Noncount: you cannot say one, two, three … It has no plural.

The next slide gives the answer.

 

Picture 1

rice

Count or noncount?

 

rice

NONCOUNT

You cannot count rice. No plural: rices

Which Word Goes With the Noun?

NounUseExample
one count nouna / ana cup · an orange
plural count nouna few · many · somea few chairs · many plates · some boxes
noncount nouna little · much · somea little juice · much cheese · some soap
Quick check: Can you count it (1, 2, 3)? Does it have a plural? Then it is a count noun. much is common in questions and negatives.
 

Look and Choose

Look at each picture. Click a, b, c, or d.

Only ONE answer is correct. The correct button turns green; a wrong button turns red.

 

1. Do you want ____ popcorn during the movie?

 

2. There is ____ apple in my lunch bag.

 

3. There are ____ pencils on the desk.

 

4. How ____ paint do we need for this wall?

 

5. I lost ____ key at the park.

 

6. How ____ spoons do we need for the party?

 

7. I only eat ____ rice at lunch.

 

8. I don't want ____ mustard on my sandwich.

 

9. Can you give me ____ egg for the cake?

11. Please bring me ____ towel. My hands are wet.

 

12. Would you like ____ tea?

 

13. I want ____ bananas for my smoothie.

 

14. My father puts ____ honey on his toast.

 

15. My neighbor has ____ ladder in his garage.

 

16. My uncle has ____ hammers in his toolbox.

18. My son wants ____ bicycle for his birthday.

 

19. The cook bought ____ new knives.

 

20. My kids want ____ spaghetti for dinner.
